title: Cryosphere Decline Exceeds Safe Planetary Limits, Study Warns
summary: Research presented at COP31 shows that climate-driven degradation of Earth's cryosphere—ice sheets, glaciers, sea ice, and permafrost—has exceeded safe planetary limits and now poses risks to conditions necessary for human society.
takeaways: Cryosphere degradation has exceeded safe planetary limits
Impacts include ice sheets, glaciers, sea ice, and permafrost
Threatens conditions necessary for human society

title: Euclid Space Telescope Releases First Major Data Set Mapping 900 Million Galaxies
summary: The Euclid space telescope released its first major data batch capturing light from more than a billion objects across an area equivalent to 9,500 full moons.

title: Earliest known quasar pair challenges black hole growth theory
summary: Astronomers discovered the earliest known compact quasar pair approximately 900 million years after the Big Bang, raising questions about rapid early supermassive black hole growth. The double system was observed with the Hubble Space Telescope during the era known as cosmic noon.
takeaways: Earliest compact quasar pair at ~900 million years post-Big Bang
Discovery challenges models of early supermassive black hole formation and rapid growth
Observed during 'cosmic noon' (peak of star and black hole formation)
Researchers used cosmological simulations spanning 10 million to 4 billion years post-Big Bang
